q: 1. The document showing the account of work done or supply of material including particulars and quantities is known as
explain: A bill is the document that records the account of work actually done or material supplied, with full particulars and quantities, used for claiming payment.

q: 2. Pick up the correct statement
options: pointing is measured in sq. m.
plastering is measured in sq. m.
glazing is measured in sq. m.
explain: Surface finishing works like pointing, plastering, and glazing are all standardly measured by area (sq. m.).

q: 3. The unit measurement of steel truss and purlin
explain: Steel trusses and purlins are structural steel items measured by weight, which can be expressed either in metric tonnes (MT) or quintals.

q: 4. The thickness of slabs and beam must be measured to the nearest
explain: As a standard estimating practice, dimensions such as slab/beam thickness are recorded correct to the nearest 0.005 m (5 mm).

q: 5. *The standard unit of measurement for expansion joint of a roof, wall or bridge etc is :
explain: Joints are linear features and are measured in running meters (rm).

q: 6. Unit of measurement of supply of brick is
explain: Bricks are discrete countable units, so their supply is measured and paid for by number (no.), typically per thousand bricks.

q: 7. *The unit rate of items written by the contractor in BOQ is in numeral as well as alphabetical form. Which one is preferred?
explain: Words (alphabetical) are preferred to prevent tampering or ambiguity with numbers in legal tender documents.

q: 8. 1 Katha equals
explain: 1 Katha, a traditional land-measurement unit used in the Terai region of Nepal/India, is equal to 3645 sq. ft.

q: 9. Which one is incorrect with respect to measurement of area of land?
explain: All the listed conversions for Bigha, Katha, and Ropani are standard accepted values in Nepal.

q: 10. 1 He = .....Ropani.
explain: One hectare is approximately equal to 19.6 Ropani.

q: 11. *An area of one hectare is equal to
explain: A hectare is a square with 100-meter sides, totaling 10,000 m^2.

q: 12. *The main target of a contractor is to
explain: While a contractor must complete the work, the primary business objective is to maximize profit.

q: 13. According to ISI method of measurement the order is in the sequence
explain: The standard sequence for recording measurements is always Length followed by Breadth (or width) and then Height (or depth/thickness).

q: 14. Tender does not contain
explain: A blank tender provided to a contractor contains items and quantities but not the rates; the contractor fills in the rates.

q: 15. The amount of money deposited along with the submission of tender is known as
explain: earnest money or bid security is deposited while bidding.

q: 16. The rate columns of a bid document is filled up by
explain: In a bid document (Bill of Quantities), the rate column against each item is filled in by the contractor while quoting the tender.

q: 17. The expenses of items which do not come under any regular head of items and the cost of unforeseen items are called
explain: Contingencies represent a percentage (usually 3-5%) of the estimate set aside for incidental or unexpected expenses.

q: 18. Liquidated damage is directly related with
explain: Liquidated damages are governed by the specific clauses and terms of the contract agreement.

q: 19. When contractor fails to complete the work, an agency is employed to execute a part or whole of the at the cost of contractor. Such an agency is known as
explain: A debitable agency is hired to complete unfinished work, and the costs incurred are debited (charged) to the original contractor's account.

q: 20. Annual financial statement of the anticipated receipts and expenditures, is called
explain: A budget is specifically the annual financial statement that anticipates (forecasts) both receipts and expenditures for a coming period.

q: 21. A fixed stated sum of penalty to be paid by contractor having definite relationship with real damage is
explain: Liquidated damages refer to a pre-agreed, fixed sum of penalty that bears a genuine, definite relationship to the actual loss/damage likely to be suffered due to delay or breach.

q: 22. The amount provided in the estimate and bill of quantities for some specialized works to be done by the specialist firm, whose details are not known at the time of preparing estimates is called:
explain: Provisional sums are amounts allocated for work that cannot be fully detailed at the time of the initial estimate.

q: 23. The rate of payment is made for 100 cu m (per % cu m) in case of
explain: Bulk earthwork items -- ordinary excavation, rock cutting, and trench excavation for foundations -- are all commonly paid on a per-100-cubic-metre (percentage cu m) basis due to their large volumes.

q: 24. The expenses of items which do not come under any regular head of items and the cost of unforeseen items are called
explain: Contingencies specifically cover the cost of unforeseen items or expenses that don't fall under any regular budget head.

q: 25. The measurement is made for stone work in square metre in case of
explain: Dressed stones used in chajjas (thin projecting slabs) are measured on an area basis, in square metres, consistent with their thin-slab nature.

q: 26. The unit of measurement of sugar is
explain: Per this table's convention, sugar (as a bulk material sometimes used in construction admixtures) is measured by volume, m³.

q: 27. The unit of measurement of electric wire
explain: Here, without diameter specification, electric wire is measured and paid for by weight, in kg, as per this table's convention.

q: 28. A fixed stated sum of penalty to be paid by contractor having no relationship with real damage in
explain: Per this table's convention, a fixed penalty sum with no direct relationship to actual damage is still labelled as liquidated damage in this specific question context.

q: 29. The unit of measurement of aluminium partition is
explain: Per this table's convention, aluminium partition work (a fabricated metal item) is measured and paid for by weight, in kg.
